name: Shivneri Fort
description: Shivneri Fort is the birthplace of the legendary Maratha emperor Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Perched atop a hill near Junnar, this fort offers panoramic views of the surrounding valleys and is a significant historical landmark.

name: Naneghat
description: An ancient mountain pass used as a trade route by the Satavahana dynasty with cave inscriptions and a water cistern. Offers breathtaking views of the Konkan coast and is famous for its reverse waterfall during monsoon.

name: Jivdhan Fort
description: A rugged hill fort near Junnar offering spectacular trekking trails and panoramic views. Associated with Maratha history and offers a challenging yet rewarding trek.

name: Chavand Fort
description: A lesser-known but historically rich fort near Junnar, associated with the Nizamshahi dynasty. Offers great trekking and panoramic views of the surrounding landscape.

name: Sindola Fort (Khireshwar)
description: Sindola Fort near Khireshwar village is a lesser-known trekking destination in the Junnar region. The fort offers stunning views of the Western Ghats and is surrounded by dense forest, making it a favourite among adventure enthusiasts.

name: Nimgiri & Hanumantgad
description: Nimgiri and Hanumantgad are twin hill forts offering a combined trekking experience in the Sahyadri range near Junnar. The forts provide spectacular views and are rich in Maratha history.

name: Hadsar Fort
description: Hadsar Fort is a challenging trek located near Junnar in the Sahyadri range. Known for its steep climb and breathtaking views of the surrounding ghats and valleys, it is popular among serious trekkers.

name: Habashi Mahal
description: A historically significant palace built by the Habashi (Abyssinian) rulers near Junnar. The structure reflects a unique blend of architectural styles and has great historical importance.

name: Ozar Ganpati Temple
description: Sri Vighnahar Ganpati at Ozar is one of the eight sacred Ashtavinayaka temples, believed to be the remover of obstacles. The temple has a golden kalash and is visited by thousands of devotees.

name: Kukdeshvar Temple
description: An ancient Shiva temple near Junnar dedicated to Lord Kukdeshvar. The temple is known for its serene surroundings and is a significant religious site for locals.

name: Kulswami Khandoba Mandir
description: Kulswami Khandoba Mandir in Vadaj is a revered local deity temple dedicated to Lord Khandoba, worshipped as the patron god of the region. The temple sees large gatherings during festivals like Champashashthi.

name: Lenyadri Caves
description: Lenyadri is a group of 30 rock-cut Buddhist caves. Cave No. 7 is dedicated to Lord Ganesha (Girijatmaj) and is one of the eight sacred Ashtavinayaka shrines. The caves date back to the 1st–3rd century CE.

name: Bhimashankar Wildlife Sanctuary
description: A biodiversity hotspot in the Sahyadri hills, home to the endangered Indian Giant Squirrel. The sanctuary also houses the famous Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga — one of the 12 sacred Shiva Jyotirlingas in India.

name: Amba Ambika Caves
description: Ancient rock-cut caves near Junnar, dedicated to Goddess Amba and Ambika. These caves are part of the large group of Buddhist cave complexes around Junnar.

name: The Tulja Caves (Tulja Lena)
description: The Tulja Caves, also known as Tulja Lena, are ancient rock-cut Buddhist caves located near Junnar. These caves feature intricately carved facades and are an important part of the Junnar cave complex heritage.

name: Malshej Ghat
description: A scenic mountain pass in the Western Ghats, famous for stunning monsoon waterfalls and flamingo sightings. A popular weekend destination from Pune and Mumbai.

name: Daryaghat
description: A scenic riverside ghat on the banks of the Kukdi River near Junnar. Famous for its reverse waterfall in monsoon season. A peaceful spot for nature lovers and a popular local picnic destination.

name: Manikdoh Dam
description: A major gravity dam constructed on the Kukadi River in Junnar taluka. The dam is a significant water reservoir for the region and is located near a Leopard Rescue Centre, making it a unique eco-tourism spot.

name: Wadaj Dam
description: An earthfill and gravity dam situated on the Meena River in Ambegaon taluka. Wadaj Dam is an important part of the regional irrigation network and offers scenic surroundings.

name: Pimpalgaon Joge Dam
description: Located on the Kukadi River, Pimpalgaon Joge Dam is notable for its significant water storage capacity. It plays a crucial role in the irrigation and water supply of the Junnar and Ambegaon region.

name: Yedgaon Dam
description: Yedgaon Dam is a picturesque dam located near Junnar. It is an important water resource for the surrounding agricultural land and offers a serene environment for visitors.

name: Dimbhe Dam
description: Dimbhe Dam is a major component of the regional irrigation network in Ambegaon taluka. Surrounded by the scenic Sahyadri hills, it is a popular picnic spot and offers stunning views of the backwaters.

name: Chilewadi Dam
description: Chilewadi Dam is a smaller dam located in the Junnar-Ambegaon region, contributing to local irrigation and water supply. It is set in peaceful natural surroundings.

name: Shiv Shrusti
description: Shiv Shrusti is an immersive theme park in Junnar dedicated to the life and legacy of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. It features life-size replicas of forts, wax statues, historical dioramas and cultural exhibits that bring Maratha history to life.

name: Narayangad Fort
description: Hill fort near Narayangaon with panoramic views of the Deccan plateau and the nearby GMRT. A short trek with ruins, water cisterns and rock-cut steps.

name: Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT), Khodad
description: One of the world's largest radio telescope arrays, with 30 dishes of 45 m each, run by NCRA-TIFR. Open to visitors on specific days.

name: Manikdoh Leopard Rescue Centre
description: Rescue and rehabilitation centre for leopards in the Junnar region, near Manikdoh Dam.

name: Habashi Gumbad
description: Historic tomb from the Bahmani/Nizamshahi era in Junnar, known for its domed Indo-Islamic architecture.

name: Ambe Hatvij
description: Scenic hill village in the Sahyadri range, known for misty viewpoints and monsoon greenery.
location: Ambe Hatvij, Junnar Taluka, Pune District
